provenance.l: Apollo 17 Mission Report JSC-07904 (Mar 1973): section 3.4, "The command module entered the atmosphere 1200 miles from the landing point"; SP-4029 timeline entry interface 301:38:38 (19:11:38 GMT 19 December 1972), drogues 301:46:22, mains 301:47:13, splashdown 301:51:59 (19:24:59 GMT; the MR prints 1925) at 17 deg 52.8 min S, 166 deg 6.6 min W (computer), 1.3 n.mi short of the target, USS Ticonderoga. Quote: "The command module landed normally and remained in the stable I attitude." Command module weight after separation 13,152 lb (5,966 kg) is an OCR reading the mission-report scan does not confirm (landing weight 12,120 lb, SP-4029)

NASA SP-4029 Apollo chronology, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" compilation (Apollo 7-17): Apollo 17 column: "Lift To Drag Ratio 0.290", "Range (n mi) 1,190" (1,190 n.mi = 2,204 km; the same cell as Apollo 16, possibly copied: the mission report says 1,200 miles), "Maximum g 6.49" (the same figure as the flight-path angle, possibly a copied cell), "Duration (sec) 801.0", velocity 36,090.3 ft/s, flight-path angle -6.49, splashdown 17.88 S 166.11 W, landing weight 12,120 lb. No Entry Postflight Analysis exists for Apollo 17 (the mission report's supplement list has none), so L/D and range are the compilation values (secondary), not a reconstruction; no first/second load-factor split is published. Model limit (US Standard Atmosphere 1976, 2026-11-25): with these inputs the model's first pulse is 6.5 g at 82 s (6.49 g flown), it dips to 2.1 g, second pulse 6.5 g; drogues 416 s (464 s flown, 301:46:22), splashdown 763 s (801 s flown). The larger pulse is within 10% of the flown maximum g; the entry runs short of the flown time, a limit of the fixed-bank planar guidance (on Apollo 11, the one flight with a published minimum, it lofts to 0.8 g between the pulses against the flown 0.48 g)
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
